pairs.difference: A: the mojito is a fully saturated green-cyan glass on a saturated royal-blue background, with an orange straw as the only warm note. Almost no neutral is left, and the lens turns the whole glass into one mint mass. B: the binoculars are muted steel-blue and the skyline has a pale pink-lavender haze, so there are quiet neutrals to rest the eye. This matches the real airplane card.
pairs.fix: Make the glass clear and nearly colorless, with grey-white highlights. Keep the drink a softer lime and calm the blue background so it is less intense than the glass.

pairs.difference: A: the witch hat is dark violet on a uniformly hot orange ring background. The card is two hue families with a heavy warm pull, and the hat's shadows sink into flat near-black purple, losing their color. B: the navy grad cap is on cyan, with a gold band and tassel as a single accent. Its shadows stay blue-violet.
pairs.fix: Use a lighter, softer orange background with some yellow variation. Paint the hat's shadow side a rich plum instead of black, and add a lighter lavender rim on the brim.

pairs.difference: B: the guitar card has too many hue families. A red body, a rainbow zigzag strap (green, orange, yellow), yellow and cyan spotlights, purple truss light and a warm wooden stage all compete, while the backdrop is a desaturated navy. A: the seahorse is orange-yellow against a single blue water field. That is one hero/background hue pair, as on the real cards.
pairs.fix: Use a plain dark strap and a single spotlight color. Leave the red guitar as the only loud color, on a calm blue stage.

pairs.difference: A: the black cat is a near-chromaless dark mass, and its shadow on the floor is a flat dull brown. Everything else (stripes, floor, eyes) is orange-yellow, so the card is almost entirely warm and has only one accent, the red collar. B: the fountain's cool cyan water and grey-beige stone contrast with the yellow stripes and warm pavers, a related hero/background split.
pairs.fix: Give the black fur cool blue-grey highlights and make the cast shadow on the floor a cool violet-brown. Add a cooler note somewhere, such as a blue-tinted floor shadow, so the card is not all orange.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is one pure saturated orange slab on saturated lawn green and sky blue. Even its side and the cross stay the same hot orange, and nothing on the card is neutral. B: the chess table is grey-lavender stone with navy and cream squares, a muted subject set against green. This matches the real lion-statue card's neutral hero.
pairs.fix: Paint the coffin as brown stained wood with darker walnut grain and a duller shaded side. Mute the grass a little so the coffin and background are not equally loud.

pairs.difference: A: a yellow duck with red and blue accents on green rays and sand. B: an orange pumpkin on muted brown-mauve wood with a purple background, and the shadow side shifts red-orange. Both have plausible local color and palette count for real cards, and color gives no clear reason to choose.

B: the candelabra card collapses to two hues, gold-tan on loud violet. The lens reads the whole brass and the candles as a single flat tan mass with no shadow color shift, and the violet background is louder than the subject. A: the oil lamp has a pale grey-white glass chimney, copper-brown brass with dark olive shadows and lime rays, so the colors are layered and related.
pairs.fix: Give the brass darker bronze-brown shadows and pale yellow highlights. Make the candles creamy white with cool grey shading, and use a softer, less intense purple background.

pairs.difference: B is the real lighthouse card. Its white bricks are a cool grey-white and its shadows go blue-grey. A: the house's stone is lavender-grey and the roof saturated purple, on a saturated green hill and blue sky. The lens reads the walls and hill as one green family, and the warm accents are lit yellow windows everywhere.
pairs.fix: Paint the stone walls a neutral cool grey with blue-grey shadows. Make the roof a duller slate purple, light only one or two windows, and mute the hill green.

pairs.difference: B: the sneakers are a neon rainbow (cobalt, lime, teal, magenta and orange laces, pink sole) on orange and yellow, about 5–6 hue families on one card. A: the gravestone is a cool blue-grey neutral on an orange wall and yellow floor, the cool-neutral-on-warm pattern of the real computer card.
pairs.fix: Limit the sneakers to blue with white soles and one accent color on the laces. Remove the pink, magenta and teal trims.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is a pure, maximum-chroma red. Shadows and folds stay the same hot red instead of shifting to crimson or wine, and the subject outshouts the cyan swirl. B: the broom is natural straw-yellow and orange-brown wood with a small red binding, at a believable local chroma on a blue wave background.
pairs.fix: Paint the scarf as red cloth with deep crimson-wine shadows in the folds and slightly pinker highlights, a bit less intense than pure red.

pairs.difference: B: the boxing gloves have red shadows and orange highlights, so the warm cast runs through the whole glove, and the wood floor is orange too. The only relief is the blue wall. A: the cauldron is muted purple-grey on a lavender floor with a pink wall, with one acid-green accent and a small fire glow. It has plenty of neutral.
pairs.fix: Shade the gloves with deep wine-red shadows and white-pink highlights instead of orange. Make the table a muted tan-brown.

pairs.difference: A: the iced tea is a saturated orange on a very loud violet background, with a hot-pink straw and a cyan umbrella. The background is the loudest area, and the ice cubes take on the orange instead of staying clear. B: the crystal ball is pale blue-white glass with gold, on a green wall and brown wood. The subject is quieter than the background and the neutral glass rests the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the ice cubes clear with cool white-grey highlights. Use a softer, darker purple background, and keep a single accent (the umbrella or the straw, not both bright).

pattern: Generated cards lose the neutrals. Grey or white parts turn cream or orange, and pure local hue is kept straight into the shadows instead of shifting to related deeper tones (crimson, plum, blue-grey). The background is pushed to the same or higher chroma as the hero. The palette then either collapses to one hot hue pair (candelabra, coffin, scarf) or fills with extra rainbow accents (sneakers, guitar strap), where real cards use one calm background, a muted or neutral area, and a single accent.
